Profile shows Capture.read calls read_range repeatedly? `_line` 6000 calls, Capture.read 12 sec for 4000 parts! Why? `Capture.read` should touch one or two parts. But read_range 3.3M calls indicates it scans many parts per read. Because I used `bisect_right(self.ends,start)` returning first part with end>start, then `while index<len(parts) and start<end`, updates start? Look at Capture.read code:
```
while index < len(self.parts) and start < end:
  ...
  result.extend(...)
  index += 1
```
It never updates `start`! So loops through all remaining parts until end of channel, but read_range only partially appends? It does extend each with a=max(start,part_start), b=min(end,part_end); for later parts a>=end so no extend, but loops O(parts). That's quadratic. Need update start = b? Cursor. Similarly fp_range never updates start! Check Capture.fp_range:
```
while index < len(parts) and start < end:
 ... a=max(start,...), b=min(end,...)
 result combine fp_range(node,...)
 index +=1
```
start never updated, but for later parts a>=end and b? `b=min(end,self.ends[index])`; a=max(start,part_start)=part_start (since part_start>end? start constant initial), b=end if part_end>end, so a may< b for each later part? Example start0,end54, after first part end14, next part start14: a=max(0,14)=14,b=min(54,27)=27 -> includes bytes14-27 (correct second), third part a=max(0,28)=28,b=min(54,41)=41 -> includes; if many more after end54, for part start55: a=max(0,55)=55,b=min(54,68)=54 -> a>b skip, but loops all. Still O(parts) per range. Capture.owners_for does cursor update correctly? It sets cursor=b and continues, so okay but while cursor<end stops after. Wait code owners_for cursor updates. Good.
Capture.read should set `start = b` after processing each part? But start is global input; if part before start etc. Simpler maintain cursor=start, use a=max(cursor,part_start), b=min(end,part_end); then cursor=b. We can also break ifcursor>=end. Similarly fp_range. This is critical performance. Fix.

Also `Capture.read` calls read_range(node, a-part_start,b-part_start, length-len(result)); if later parts after end, b may negative? no. But cursor.

Implement:
```
cursor=start
while index<len and cursor<end:
 a=max(cursor,starts[index]); b=min(end,ends[index])
 if a<b: read...; cursor=b
 index++
```
Need index progression through zero parts. If b<a for zero, still index++. cursor remains.
For `fp_range` same.
Maybe `owners_for` already cursor but uses `while index... cursor<end` and a=max(cursor,part_start), b=min(end,part_end), cursor=b. yes.
Fix. Then rerun profile/scaling.
